When you're using Comcast and connect to SiteInTheMiddleOfTheDesert.com, Comcast does not send your traffic to that site themselves. Go into the command prompt on your computer (start->cmd) and type: "tracert alibaba.com" without the quotes. What that will do is show you the path for your computer to get to alibaba, a trade site hosted in China. Each of those numbers is your packet of data hopping from one router to another.

What you'll notice is that your packets leave your ISP's routers extremely quickly. And the only ISP routers you go through are generally going to be very [relatively] close to you. ISP's work as middle men, don't really deliver the internet to you but instead pass data along to other routers that they don't own. The internet is one giant cooperative with companies and organizations worldwide working together to process and send data along just so we have this great system that we do have. No single company sends your data directly from the middle of America to the middle of the Sahara themselves. It'd be not only technologically impossible (signals decay over time) but unfathomably expensive.

At the time, the connection between the Netflix's ISP and Comcast was getting full and Comcast subscribers were complaining to Netflix about he quality of the connection. Netflix's ISP approached Comcast about adding capacity to their cross-connect and were told that it would be to costly. The ISP offered to cover the cost of any upgrades and were told that it was not sufficient.

Netflix approached Comcast and offered them a free connection to their CDN (content distribution network), which is a network that Netflix pays for to get their content as close to their subscribers as possible. They also offered to freely install a Netflix cache node that would reduce load on Comcast's connections by serving the content internally. Netflix was told those would not do.

Comcast continued to let their customers have shitty service to the content they wanted for months, knowing that the shitty service would drive people away from Netflix. At which point they basically added the cross connects the ISP wanted in the first place and everything was working fine again.
